drills.q: Why do optimistic rollups use a ~7-day challenge window, and what actually enforces it?
drills.a: Window = max time for an honest verifier to detect fraud and litigate the dispute game down to one on-chain-executed instruction. Enforcement: L1 bridge refuses finalization until expiry; any challenger can slash via valid fraud proof; Arbitrum BoLD (Feb 2025) made challenging permissionless.

drills.q: Contrast 1-of-N honest vs 0-of-N trust assumptions across optimistic and ZK rollups.
drills.a: Optimistic: safety holds if at least ONE honest party watches every assertion and challenges in-window - liveness is social/economic. ZK: zero watchers needed - validity proofs verified mechanically by L1 math; invalid transitions cannot finalize even with universal operator collusion. ZK pays prover costs upfront for this.

drills.q: Walk through a bisection-based fraud proof resolution.
drills.a: Challenger disputes post-batch root; both submit intermediate roots at successive halves of execution until they disagree about exactly ONE step; on-chain mini-interpreter re-executes that single step and declares winner; loser's bond pays challenger. Total L1 work O(log steps) - that amortization is what makes optimism cheap.

drills.q: Lay out Vitalik's zkEVM type taxonomy with tradeoffs.
drills.a: Type 1: full Ethereum-equivalence (verifies L1 itself) - slowest proving. Type 2: EVM-equivalence (Scroll/Taiko class). Type 2.5: gas tweaks for proving ease. Type 3: some precompiles removed. Type 4: language-level compile to zk-IR (zkSync Era) - fastest proofs, bytecode-level tooling breaks. Compatibility falls as prover cost falls.

drills.q: What did blobs change for rollup economics, and what does pruning mean?
drills.a: Dencun (3/13/2024): dedicated blob market - ~128 KiB each, own fee curve, pruned after ~4096 epochs (~18 days). L2 fees fell roughly an order of magnitude overnight. Pruning = consensus guarantees availability only through the settlement/challenge window; long-term archival shifts to rollups/indexers by design.

drills.q: Blob supply trajectory: targets/maxes from Dencun through BPO2.
drills.a: Dencun 3/6 (3/2024); Pectra 6/9 (5/7/2025); Fusaka PeerDAS (12/3/2025) then BPO1 10/15 (12/9/2025), BPO2 14/21 (1/7/2026). PeerDAS: erasure-code into 128 columns + sampling gives ~8x headroom toward 48 blobs without per-node load growth.

drills.q: Rank Ronin, Wormhole, Nomad by root cause and name each design lesson.
drills.a: Ronin $624M (3/2022): 5-of-9 validator keys phished by Lazarus - committees are key-management problems. Wormhole $325M (2/2022): deprecated sig-verification path accepted forged guardian signatures - where signatures ARE trust, sig bugs are fatal; Jump recapitalized. Nomad $190M (8/2022): initialization let zero proofs validate - copy-paste free-for-all; lesson: adversarial init vectors. All: 2022 saw $2B+ across 13 bridges.

drills.q: Design a bridge between two EVM chains you don't control.
drills.a: Light-client contracts verifying other chain's consensus (headers or ZK-proven consensus attestations), message passing with Merkle inclusion proofs against posted roots, replay nonces, per-asset rate limits with anomaly throttling, governance timelock for client updates separate from pauser multisig, monitoring on mint events. Never: small attestation committees above insured value.

drills.q: Sequencer goes down for two hours on your L2. What happens to funds and why isn't it catastrophic?
drills.a: UX freezes; funds don't move - sequencing controls ordering, not custody. Users retain forced-inclusion via L1 inbox; withdrawals resume when sequencer returns or via escape hatches. Real risks are fairness: MEV extraction, soft censorship. Real fixes: hardened forced inclusion, shared sequencers (Espresso), based rollups.

drills.q: CTO asks: general rollup vs app-specific rollup vs appchain. Give the decision tree.
drills.a: General-purpose (Base/Arbitrum) if composability with liquidity matters and ops burden must stay low. App-rollup (Orbit/CDK/zkStack) if custom fee tokens, dedicated blockspace, sovereignty over upgrades, and infra staffing exist. Appchain only with consensus-level needs AND token-funded security. Always price: liquidity fragmentation, bridge exposure, stage/decentralization compliance.

drills.q: Validium vs rollup for a high-value exchange product? Justify.
drills.a: Exchange already holds custody keys, so validium's committee adds marginal trust risk while cutting DA costs dramatically - defensible internally. For anything market-facing: default full rollup; committee withholding freezes assets (availability risk), fatal for leveraged positions. Volitions allow per-account choice.

drills.q: Explain how PeerDAS sampling preserves security as blob count scales.
drills.a: Each blob erasure-coded into 128 columns; nodes custody a subset (scaled by validator count) and randomly sample others. k successful samples imply >=50% data exists with overwhelming probability -> full reconstruction possible. Per-node verification stays constant while network capacity grows toward 48 blobs; new failure surface = custodial coverage during correlated churn.
